newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends off, bearish inventory data seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends off, bearish inventory data seen.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower Tuesday ahead of weekly oil inventory data which is expected to show another bearishly large build in distillate stocks, traders said.
"The selling we saw was ahead of the APIs. A bearish build is expected for distillates, and that's enough to bring things down," said a trader.
December heating oil settled off 0.53 cent at 65.42 cents a gallon while December gasoline ended 0.39 cent lower at 64.61 cents a gallon. December crude settled 15 cents lower at $22.64 a barrel.
Heating oil is a component of total distillate stocks.
Traders expected the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a build of about 2.5 million barrels for the week ended November 1 in its oil inventory data released Tuesday evening.
For the week ended October 25, the API said distillate stocks grew 3.6 million barrels.

Refiners have been pumping out distillate at a record pace to meet winter heating oil demand after distillate stocks stood at historical lows throughout the summer. Distillate output is being maximized at the expense of gasoline when seasonal refinery maintenance is cutting gasoline output.
Gasoline inventories are now hovering at 20-year lows, and refiners have been buying gasoline in the U.S. Gulf cash market this week to insure demand is met, dealers said.
"I think gasoline acted pathetic given the strength in today's cash market," said one trader of Tuesday's action in gasoline prices.

Doctors for Russian President Boris Yeltsin declared his heart bypass operation a complete success Tuesday, but traders said the news was neutral to oil prices as it was another sign the Russian government would not be disrupted.
Russia is one of the world's largest oil producers.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
